toegepas.blok: Rekenaars wat 'n hele kamer gevul het
toegepas.voor: 'n hele kamer gevul van die een muur tot die ander
toegepas.na: 'n hele kamer van die een muur tot die ander gevul
toegepas.rede_vinder: In Afrikaans the adverbial phrase naturally comes before the past participle at the end of the clause; the word count stays the same.
toegepas.fout: The prepositional phrase trails after the past participle 'gevul', which reads as spoken rather than written Afrikaans word order.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Putting the participle at the end of the clause is the standard written order, the word count stays the same and the meaning does not change.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'hou ... op' can be misread as the separable verb 'ophou' (stop); 'bewaar' says 'keep' unambiguously, and the word count stays the same.
toegepas.fout: 'hou ... op rekenaars' is a loose verb for storing information and can briefly read as the separable verb 'ophou'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'bewaar' is the exact verb for keeping information, adds no words and says the same thing.

toegepas.voor: Besighede kan goed koop by en verkoop aan mense in ander lande
toegepas.na: Besighede kan goed by mense in ander lande koop en aan hulle verkoop
toegepas.rede_vinder: Stranded prepositions ('koop by en verkoop aan mense') copy the English 'buy from and sell to'; Afrikaans puts each preposition with its own object (one word more).
toegepas.fout: 'koop by en verkoop aan mense' leaves two prepositions stranded before one object, copying English 'buy from and sell to'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Giving each preposition its own object is natural Afrikaans with the same people, actions and meaning, and the one extra word keeps the lesson at 449 of 450.

vlae.teks: Hospitale, banke en winkels werk elke dag hiermee. / Skole en laboratoriums hou hulle inligting op rekenaars.
vlae.rede: The first five items are 'Om ...' purposes that answer the heading, but the last two are full sentences about who uses computers, so the list stops matching its heading; 'hiermee' also has no antecedent inside its own item. Fixing this means rewording the content of the items, so it is flagged, not changed.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Hoe rekenaars kleiner en makliker geword het
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Hulle het makliker geword om te gebruik met knoppies en prente op 'n skerm
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Knoppies en prente op 'n skerm het hulle makliker gemaak om te gebruik
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The trailing 'met knoppies ...' phrase is wooden; making the buttons and pictures the subject reads naturally with the same word count.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original fits the paragraph's 'het ... geword' chain, and the proposal ('het hulle makliker gemaak om te gebruik') is itself English-shaped, so it is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Two coordinate adjectives before a noun are separated by a comma.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The comma between these adjectives is optional, so the glossary definition has no fault, and it may be shared with other lessons, so it must not get a second wording.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: totdat 'n skip hulle oor die see neem
laat_vaar_vorige.na: totdat 'n skip hulle oor die see geneem het
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The sentence is in the past (Vroeer het ... gewag), so the subordinate clause needs the past form too; this adds one word.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: A present-tense verb in a 'totdat' clause after a past main clause is normal Afrikaans, so the original is not wrong, and the change adds a word to a lesson already at its ceiling.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: wat vir jou bladsye oor 'n onderwerp opspoor
laat_vaar_vorige.na: wat bladsye oor 'n onderwerp vir jou opspoor
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'vir jou bladsye' can be misread as 'your pages'; moving 'vir jou' removes the ambiguity without adding words.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Putting 'vir jou' before the object is natural Afrikaans word order and does not read as 'your pages'; this is a lateral reordering of a shared glossary definition.
